label: Supervenience as a requirement of…: The constraint that competent moral judgments must not morally…
term: supervenience as a requirement of linguistic competence
definition: The constraint that competent moral judgments must not morally distinguish items without a nonmoral difference. Blackburn explains the conceptual requirement from the guiding purposes of moral talk. In the test this is one primitive explanation edge from purposesOfMoralTalk to supervenienceRequirement. It does not assert a complete supervenience semantics, exclude other explanations, or yield a metaphysical truthmaker.

formal_gap.meaning: SupervenienceExplainedByPurposesReading Explains purposes constraint says that the purposes of moral talk explain the conceptual requirement that competent moral judgments not distinguish items without a nonmoral difference (Blackburn, as SEP §3.4 reports). Its body is one edge of the supplied relation Explains.
examples: Blackburn's explanation: because moral talk serves to guide choice, a competent speaker does not assign different moral verdicts to two cases that are identical in every nonmoral respect.
exclusions: A complete supervenience semantics or a metaphysical truthmaker.
The exclusion of other explanations: it records one edge only.
open_obligations: Explains is supplied; no structural law (asymmetry, transitivity) is assumed.
No formalization candidate: the explanatory relation is the supplied parameter.
